There is a danger of falling into the oil containments pit when working near 
 large power transformers.

There is danger of falling off the top of the transformer when cleaning 
 insulator, wear safety belt.
Digital Avometer, test plug, and test leads.

Determine that the oil level in the transformer tank and all liquid filled 
 compartments, such as junction boxes or switches, is satisfactory.

Test the dielectric strength of the Oil from the tank bottom that tests, check 
 often based upon need.
Clean all bushings if dirty, and inspect the porcelain for cracks.

Check temperature gauge, liquid level gauges, pressure gauges, and other 
 indicators. Record results.

Carryout the Megger check or power factor check of insulation for comparison 
 with 
 previous observations.

Clean fan blades and check fan operation by turning control switch to 
 "Manual".

Make certain that no tools or other objects have been left in or on ,the 
 transformer.

text:
Power Stations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document outlines the equipment inspection I1 on Coupling 
 Transformer 6.6/6.6KV, which must be performed on yearly bases as 
 indicated by Y1 in the title block.
Technical 
 Specification
3 phase Transformer
Rated power | 8 MVA | Type of tap changer | off 
 load
Rated frequency | 50HZ | Weight of oil | 4.2 ton
Rated voltage | LV 6.6 KV, HV 6.6 KV | Weight of transformer (with oil ) | 18.5 ton
Type of cooling: | ONAN / ONAF |  | 
Winding connection | Yn1 delta |  | 
The first 
 draft initiated by eng. Ashraf Kamal Oshbah, tested by eng. Reda 
 Ragab Karam, accepted by general manager eng. Hamdy Dorgam, approved by eng. 
 Gaber Mohamed Farahat head sector of Damanhour power station and certified by eng. 
 Sania Diab Attia Diab : WDEPC Inspection head sector 
 and MPIS coordinator.
Safety Precautions
A 
 work permit must be issued.
The 
 qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable ID safety category.
Safety 
 fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required.
Wear 
 safety and healthy equipments as safety helmet, safety shoes, ... etc
The transformer must be was isolated and proper grounding is required.
There is a danger of falling into the oil containments pit when working near 
 large power transformers.
There is danger of falling off the top of the transformer when cleaning 
 insulator, wear safety belt.
Tools and Equipment
Complete tool set.
Digital Avometer, test plug, and test leads.
Meager device.
Blower or vacuum cleaner.
PVC Ladder - Brushes.
Work to be Carried Out
Determine that the oil level in the transformer tank and all liquid filled 
 compartments, such as junction boxes or switches, is satisfactory.
Test the dielectric strength of the Oil from the tank bottom that tests, check 
 often based upon need.
Clean all bushings if dirty, and inspect the porcelain for cracks.
Check the pressure relief device.
Check temperature gauge, liquid level gauges, pressure gauges, and other 
 indicators. Record results.
Carryout the Megger check or power factor check of insulation for comparison 
 with 
 previous observations.
Clean fan blades and check fan operation by turning control switch to 
 "Manual".
Check paint on thank and accessories and repaint when required.
Make certain that no tools or other objects have been left in or on ,the 
 transformer.
Check cables tighten.
